paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Jesus is not hard to reach, even when He's trying to lie low. He goes into a house in the region of Tyre, not wanting anyone to know He's there, and He is unable to escape their notice (Mark 7:24). I sat in the back of a junk drawer for years and nobody found me, so a Jesus who gets found in one little house is good news to me. Whoever you are and wherever you come from, you can come to Him, like this Greek woman who kept asking (Mark 7:26).

Look at what Jesus says to her: "Because of this answer, you may go. The demon has left your daughter" (Mark 7:29). She didn't have the perfect words, she had a humble, hanging-on kind of faith, and she got her little girl back (Mark 7:30). I have shown up to the oven with a half-baked plan more times than I can count, so this one encourages me, friend. Keep coming to Jesus, keep asking, and keep trusting Him when the answer doesn't look like what you expected.

The deaf man's story shows what Jesus does for people who are brought to Him. Some people begged Jesus to place His hand on the man, and Jesus opened what was closed, his ears and his tongue (Mark 7:32-35). The people were utterly astonished and said, "He has done all things well!" (Mark 7:37). So here's your takeaway, baker: bring your people to Jesus, bring yourself too, and trust that whatever He does, He does well.
